description:
## Problem
mcp-result-parity-test-ci-timeout-20261116 was closed when BenchBox #4316 merged (2026-11-18T14:13:47Z). Its last acceptance point, 10 consecutive CI runs of the shipped-defaults case under half the 60 s per-test timeout, could only be measured after merge. This item records that measurement.

## Baseline
Before #4316, 12 trunk runs: shipped-defaults 28.4-57.3 s (median 42.1), compression-disabled 11.2-21.4 s, polars-df 28.2-49.2 s. Locally under the host lock after the change: shipped-defaults 9.3 s.

## Method
Take the first 10 medium-tier runs on develop after #4316's merge commit that contain `tests/integration/test_cli_mcp_result_parity.py` (trunk.yml medium shards, or ci.yml medium-test jobs on develop pushes). Read each case's duration from the job log's `--durations=25` section; if the test is no longer in the slowest 25, record that as an upper bound equal to the 25th entry's time. If the weekly duration refresh (tests/fixtures/medium_shard_durations.json) has a newer measurement, record it too. Record run ids and per-case seconds in context.

## Decision gate
- All 10 under 30 s for every case: finish.
- Any case at or over 30 s, or any timeout: do not raise the timeout. Reopen investigation in a new item with the run ids, the per-phase timing (dbgen, compression, MCP half), and the runner class.

## Guardrails
- Read-only: no code changes, no re-runs dispatched solely to collect samples (they compete for shared runners and the REST quota).
- Do not change the 60 s timeout or the test's markers.
- Never infer a duration that the log does not show; record the bound and its source.

## Verification rubric
Pass if context lists 10 consecutive qualifying develop runs after the merge commit, each with run id and per-case seconds (or a stated upper bound), all under 30 s. Fail or follow-up otherwise.
